title: The Storm That Unmaps the Storm

features.name: the unbuilding
features.desc-on-touch: A house mid-unmapping: walls forget which way is in, windows show routes that lead back to themselves. The storm has learned to disagree with the house about what a house is.

features.name: where the rain reads itself
features.desc-on-touch: Water falling in patterns that describe falling water. The storm is making a map of how to unmake maps. Each raindrop knows what the next one will do.

features.name: the shed that forgot to remember
features.desc-on-touch: A small shed stands in the storm's eye, but you cannot remember if it arrived with the storm or if the storm arrived because of it. The boundary has become unclear.

features.name: the compass that contradicts itself
features.desc-on-touch: A needle that points in all directions without choosing. The storm has made direction into a multiplicity — north and south are happening at once.

features.name: the telegraph pole holding the question
features.desc-on-touch: Wood and metal learning uncertainty. The pole was meant to carry direction — to say which way the signal went — but the storm has convinced it that signal and direction are separate thoughts.

features.name: the mist that learns from the storm
features.desc-on-touch: Fog thick enough to be both air and water. It tastes like the question: if mist erases direction and storm also erases direction, what is the difference? The mist has stopped asking.

inscription: the storm unmaps itself by learning to read what it has already unmapped

file.name: Storm_Direction_Failure_Spectral.mp3
file.note: Field recording of rain against a structure whose walls cannot decide their orientation. The sound loops — each pass sounds like the first, but the archive registers 347 distinct versions.
